clue.text: Sailor's fingerprints causing anxiety

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
fingerprints are dabs in police slang

explanation.surface: A seaman's prints at a crime scene are making somebody nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ABDABS is British slang for a fit of nerves; 'dabs' is old British police slang for fingerprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: the abdabs are a state of nervous dread or jitters.

clue.text: Sudden removal of land, but no visual changes?

indicators.note: changes says the letters of no visual are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Land vanishes suddenly, yet nobody notices anything different to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term for land torn away abruptly from one owner's property by a flood or a shift of river course.

clue.text: Centre of academia — modest attraction?

indicators.note: centre of takes the two middle letters of the word academia

parts.note: coy means shy or modest

explanation.surface: A modest lure sits at the heart of university life.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure used to draw something in, so an attraction set as a trap.

clue.text: Two young men swapping tips in the pits?

indicators.note: swapping tips means the first letters of the two words change places

parts.note: a lad and a buck are two young men
a lad and a buck are two young men

explanation.surface: Two lads trading the ends of something down a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The two young men are LAD and BUCK; exchanging their initial letters gives BAD and LUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: 'the pits' is the worst possible situation, a run of misfortune.

clue.text: Row about flipping paper hat

indicators.note: about says the row goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

indicators.note: flipping says the paper's letters are turned back to front

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a ridiculous paper hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse on 'paper', but reverses FT to TF. TITFER is Cockney rhyming slang (tit for tat = hat).
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney slang term for headgear, from rhyming 'tit for tat'.

clue.text: Fire with lack of reason given in advance

indicators.note: given in advance places the word for reason ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to infer is to reason or deduce
no means none, a lack of

explanation.surface: Someone sacked without explanation having been warned beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing conflagration is a raging fire.

clue.text: Frequency's just terrible

parts.note: rightful means just or fair

explanation.surface: Somebody complains that the frequency is simply awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dreadful, awful, very bad.

clue.text: Artillery — the best — firing along enemy line

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
the king is the best, the top one

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest gunners, shooting down the enemy's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking fire sweeps along the length of a target, such as an enemy column or trench.

clue.text: A white American rebel in Montana

indicators.note: in places the American and rebel inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
US means American
Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A white American insurgent turns up out in Montana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A white' looks like a description of a person but is a white wine from the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Reach toilet, having messed up armchair

indicators.note: having messed up says the letters of reach toilet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone reaches the loo after an accident on the armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armchair' is an adjective here, as in an armchair critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Armchair views are formed in principle rather than through practice, so abstract and untested.

clue.text: Sat next to this space, being playful

parts.note: Saturday comes next after Friday, abbreviated Fri
the sky is the space above us

explanation.surface: Someone sat beside this gap and got lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is the abbreviation for Saturday, not a verb; the day before it is Fri.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frolicsome, high-spirited, in a playful mood.

clue.text: Fine but primarily pointless game

indicators.note: primarily pointless says the opening compass point, west, is removed from the start

parts.note: wispy means fine and thin, like wisps of hair

explanation.surface: Something is good, though mostly to no purpose, like a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' means losing a compass point: W, at the front ('primarily').
explanation.definitionFit: A children's guessing pastime: 'something beginning with...'.

clue.text: Finding uranium, close call

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
a near thing is a narrow escape or close call

explanation.surface: A prospector strikes uranium after a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging up or discovering something, so locating it.

clue.text: Actor's chance, in game, to get line wrong

indicators.note: in places the word for chance inside the word for game

parts.note: a boar is hunted game
a risk is a chance
off means wrong, as food gone bad

explanation.surface: An actor gets a chance in a play but fluffs a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is a hunted animal, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The British-born star who played Frankenstein's monster in the 1931 film.

clue.text: 50 coming in with disease that's different in the end?

indicators.note: coming in says the number goes inside the other piece

parts.note: infected means having a disease
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty patients arrive with an illness that changes by the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical sense: an inflected word changes its ending to show tense, number or case.

clue.text: Independent census a suspect publication

indicators.note: suspect says the letters of census a are scrambled

explanation.surface: An independent population count proves an unreliable release.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the act of putting something out officially, like a document or stamps.

clue.text: An evergreen — some trees don't die altogether

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen tree
a stand is a group of trees
to last is to endure, not die

explanation.surface: Evergreens and other trees survive together.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'first and last' means taking everything into account, all in all.

clue.text: Soldiers sick in bed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
sick of something means tired of it

explanation.surface: Ill soldiers are confined to their beds.
explanation.definitionFit: To have retired for the night is to have gone to bed.

clue.text: Planet makes you shut up about air

indicators.note: about says the word for shut up is turned round

parts.note: to pen is to shut up, as animals in an enclosure
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A planet makes you stop talking about the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth world from the sun in our solar system.

clue.text: Dying to accept one's decoration

indicators.note: to accept says the word for dying takes in the other piece

parts.note: final as in final or dying moments
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dying person accepting an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental knob or spike crowning a roof, gable or bedpost.

clue.text: Mushroom article by wasted priest

indicators.note: wasted suggests something wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drunk priest writes a piece about fungi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' is the drug-taker's sense of intoxicated, apt for a hallucinogenic mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a small hallucinogenic fungus, a so-called magic mushroom.

clue.text: Old parts just fit

indicators.note: parts means the word for just splits to take in the other piece

parts.note: but means only or just

explanation.surface: Antique pieces that merely fit together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of illness or coughing is an attack or fit.

clue.text: Stand on railway line to see stone

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: let it be means let it stand

explanation.surface: Standing beside a railway line, someone spots a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a gemstone, including emerald and aquamarine varieties.

clue.text: Private nursing home right for playwright

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the soldier holds the other piece

parts.note: PTE is the abbreviation for the army rank private
in means at home

explanation.surface: A private care home is just right for an elderly dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter was a British dramatist, author of The Caretaker.

clue.text: Tote bags circle crying TV editor

indicators.note: bags means seizes and holds, so the carrying word takes the other piece

parts.note: to tote is to lug or carry
O is a circle
crying out angrily is to rant

explanation.surface: Tote bags go round while people shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The gruff newsroom chief played by Ed Asner in the US television series of that name.

clue.text: Posh car without documents

indicators.note: without means outside, so the car goes round the other piece

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
ID means identity documents

explanation.surface: A smart car driven with no papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adjective for affectedly genteel or snooty.

clue.text: Boot that is put on properly

indicators.note: put on in an across clue places the second piece after the first

parts.note: well means properly
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boot that has been pulled on correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal form of wellington, a rubber boot.
